headline: Law extends the Congressional Award Board through 2028 and drops the required metals for youth award medals.
what_it_does: This law keeps the Congressional Award Board running through fiscal year 2028. The board runs the Congressional Award Program, which gives medals to young people ages 14 to 23 who meet goals in public service, personal development, and physical fitness. The law also removes a rule that the medals must be made of gold-plate over bronze, rhodium over bronze, or bronze. The extension counts back to October 1, 2023, when the last authorization ran out.

who_it_affects.how: They can keep earning Congressional Award medals through the program until at least fiscal year 2028.
The board is legally authorized again, with no gap since October 1, 2023, and no longer has to use specific metals for medals.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 26, 2025, but treated as if it took effect October 1, 2023; authorization runs through fiscal year 2028.
